groups.title: Tablet (E80900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 3 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 2/3 to 2 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Take it at bedtime or on an empty stomach. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or reduce the amount gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger; if you have an acute abdominal disease such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis; if you have intestinal obstruction; or if you have a hereditary problem such as Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are on a sodium-restricted diet, if you have kidney impairment, if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian, and unless it is really necessary children aged 10 years or younger should avoid taking it. Do not chew the tablets. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Avoid taking an antacid or drinking milk within 1 hour after taking this medicine.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, abdominal discomfort, cramps, diarrhoea or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (E60500ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for regulating the bowel, constipation, loose stools, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and abnormal fermentation in the intestine.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are under treatment by a doctor.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E35700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, a feeling of a blocked stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid eructation (sour belching), loss of appetite, indigestion, overeating, promotion of digestion, and a feeling of fullness in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger, if you are receiving dialysis, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment, if you have an allergic constitution, or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a tetracycline antibiotic.

If constipation or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Solution (A26800ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for mental fatigue and asthenia (weakness) that appear with loss of appetite, and for wasting diseases.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle in 1 day, in the morning on an empty stomach. Remove the plastic cap, press the cap to drop the powder into the vial, shake it to dissolve the powder well and then take it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if the user is a child aged 12 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

This medicine may cause mild excitement or insomnia, so do not take it at night. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

If abdominal pain or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (B41000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: There is a daytime tablet and a night-time tablet. For the daytime tablet, ages 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet per dose; ages 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 2 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals. For the night-time tablet, 6 hours after taking the daytime tablet, ages 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet per dose; ages 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes); or cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (D46400ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough, sputum and asthma.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 10 mL per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 6.67 mL per dose. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: 5 mL per dose. Ages 5 years to under 8 years: 3.33 mL per dose. Ages 3 years to under 5 years: 2.5 mL per dose. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 2 mL per dose. Take it 5 to 6 times in 1 day, at intervals of about 4 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or a high fever; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if the user is under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For babies and young children aged 7 years or younger, give a syrup preparation instead. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (123840ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum (phlegm) in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, bronchiectasis and pharyngitis, for drainage of pus in chronic sinusitis, and for drainage in exudative otitis media (middle ear inflammation).
groups.usage: Ages 6 years to 12 years: take 250 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 2 years to 5 years: take 250 to 500 mg in 1 day, divided into 4 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment or heart impairment, if you have had gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

If it is taken together with an antibiotic or with a syrup containing trimetoquinol hydrochloride, take them separately.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely nausea, vomiting, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, gastrointestinal bleeding or heartburn; occasionally loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or thirst; in sensitive people stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth); occasionally rash, erythema (red patches) or eczema; rarely headache; in sensitive people rhinitis; occasionally itching, palpitations, runny nose or a feeling of pressure over the whole body; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); signs of shock; anaphylaxis; a cough lasting 14 days or more; liver function disorder with raised AST, ALT, ALP or LDH; or jaundice.

groups.title: Syrup (172840ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) per dose. Ages 7 to 10 years: 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) per dose. Ages 3 to 6 years: 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) per dose. Ages 1 to 2 years: 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) per dose. Take it 3 to 4 times in 1 day. In children weighing less than 30 kg the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg (25 mL), and it is better to avoid giving it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy or are breast-feeding; if you are being given high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Do not take more than the recommended dose.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed, liver cirrhosis, liver impairment, kidney impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant; or if you have chickenpox.

When it is taken for a cold, as a rule take it for no more than 5 days; without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Do not take this medicine together with high-dose methotrexate given as cancer treatment or with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking low-dose aspirin, an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation or black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function or liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema or purpura; visual disturbance, deafness, tinnitus, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral oedema.
